Paragraph: In Bhagavad Gita Chapter 6, Verses 16-17, Krishna teaches moderation: 'Yoga is not possible for one who eats too much or eats too little, nor for one who sleeps too much or stays awake too long. But for one who is moderate in eating, recreation, work, and sleep, Yoga destroys all sorrow.'
Situation/Problem_Faced: Extreme lifestyle habits, burnout, poor sleep hygiene, and physical self-neglect causing mental suffering.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna emphasizes Yuktahara-Vihara (balanced lifestyle), advocating moderation in diet, rest, work, and recreation.
Outcome/Resolution: Adopting a balanced lifestyle reduces physical stress and supports mental stability.
Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The Gita teaches moderation in all aspects of life as the foundation for inner peace and spiritual growth.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Parallels lifestyle psychiatry and behavioral medicine, emphasizing sleep, nutrition, and work-rest balance.
